name: Dagger

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

modes.label: Cloud Engines (hosted, early access)
modes.note: Hosted Dagger Engines that run Cloud Checks on Git push/PR ('auto-scaled on Cloud Engines'). Metered in core minutes; price unpublished; early access via Discord. CI runners, not interactive sandboxes.

plans.name: Individual
plans.note: Observability for 1 user; 1,000,000 monthly events; 1-month run history; community support. No hosted compute included.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: Flat $50/month after a 2-week trial for up to 10 users (not per seat); 10,000,000 monthly events; 1-year run history; Module Insights + Catalog; email support. Overage above the events cap is unpublished.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom; SSO, managed single-tenant deployment, 24/7 premium support.

caveats: Dagger Cloud plans (Individual free / Team $50 per month flat for up to 10 users / Enterprise custom) are 'EARLY ACCESS' observability + module-sharing plans capped by monthly telemetry events (1M / 10M). Hosted compute now exists separately as Cloud Engines (used by Cloud Checks, early access), metered in core minutes, but no price is published. The self-hosted engine is free.
Inventory exclusion: CI engine/cloud observability, not hosted CPU. Card contains no numeric compute modes and no selectable price plan.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.verification: GitHub integration; early access via Discord for Cloud Engines
fleet.tiers: Individual 1 user / Team 10 users / Enterprise custom
fleet.notes: No hosted-compute quotas published; Cloud Engines are early access.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Package the container state as an OCI image, and publish it to a registry
snapshot_on_demand.note: Container.publish / export: filesystem state only (no memory). Dagger Container values are immutable, so any intermediate state can be reused to start new containers (fork-like); published images can boot new containers. Not a VM snapshot.

own_agent_api.quote: Sending to a never-started agent starts it (signal-with-start).
own_agent_api.note: EXPERIMENTAL core Agent API (spawn/send/pause/resume/wait/notify/stop/reseed; conversation snapshot readable as an LLM value) drives Dagger's OWN LLM agent loop running in the engine, with containers as tools. Does not drive Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode inside a container. container-use is the reverse direction (an MCP server that external agents like Claude Code call).

harness_api.quote: Sending to a never-started agent starts it (signal-with-start).
harness_api.note: EXPERIMENTAL core Agent API (spawn/send/pause/resume/wait/notify/stop/reseed; conversation snapshot readable as an LLM value) drives Dagger's OWN LLM agent loop running in the engine, with containers as tools. Does not drive Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode inside a container. container-use is the reverse direction (an MCP server that external agents like Claude Code call).

ingress_rules.quote: Creates a tunnel that forwards traffic from the caller's network to this service.
ingress_rules.note: Services are reachable only by clients inside the Dagger session ('Configures a hostname which can be used by clients within the session to reach this container.') unless explicitly tunneled (Service.up / `dagger up`) with chosen frontend/backend port mappings to the caller's machine. No public URLs.

secret_proxy.quote: injects actual values as environment variables in the container
secret_proxy.note: Dagger secrets (env:, file:, cmd:, vault://, op://, aws+sm://, gcp://, libsecret://) are resolved on the host and injected INTO the container via withSecretVariable (env) or withMountedSecret (file). Safeguards are only log redaction, never written to layers, excluded from cache keys; container-use additionally hides values from the model's context, but the sandbox process holds the real secret. Engine-side non-HTTP uses keep the credential out of the container: withRegistryAuth (registry push) and sshfsVolume privateKey.

volume_attach.quote: Constructs an engine-managed volume backed by operator-provided storage beneath the configured engine state root.
volume_attach.note: Container.withMountedVolume (optional readOnly) mounts a Volume: engineVolume (operator-provided storage on the engine) or sshfsVolume (remote SSHFS). Also CacheVolume (withMountedCache) persisting across runs.

volume_shared.quote: Shares the cache volume amongst many build pipelines
volume_shared.note: CacheVolume sharing mode SHARED (default, read-write across concurrent pipelines), LOCKED (serializes writes) or PRIVATE. Volumes can be mounted read-only. Scope is one engine (self-hosted or Cloud Engine).

isolation.quote: containers, including nested engines, are in sibling `/buildkit` cgroups.
isolation.note: The Dagger Engine executes pipeline steps as OCI containers via an embedded BuildKit/runc backend (shared-kernel container isolation), not full VMs/microVMs.

image_oci.quote: Package the container state as an OCI image, and publish it to a registry
image_oci.note: Container.from() starts from any OCI/Docker image; Container.publish/export produce OCI images.

docker_inside.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI. It makes your pipelines faster and more repeatable... spin up multi-container environments just in time
docker_inside.note: Dagger runs and composes containers itself via its engine (buildkit/runc); running a nested full Docker daemon (docker-in-docker) inside a Dagger container is not a documented, supported first-class feature and no docs on privileged/insecure dind mode were found.

nested_virt.quote: The missing software stack for CI
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Dagger is a container-based CI/pipeline engine, no /dev/kvm or nested VM support documented.

desktop.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

browser.quote: Run Playwright browser tests, wired to the service under test.
browser.note: Dagger offers a Playwright test-runner module (browsers as ephemeral test tooling inside a pipeline container), not a managed/persistent browser product for agent browsing. not offered: outside the product's scope

computer_use.quote: The missing software stack for CI
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

anti_bot.quote: The missing software stack for CI
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

captcha_solving.quote: The missing software stack for CI
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

ssh.quote: --engine string      Select the engine: cloud, image://, container://, tcp://, tls://, ssh://, kube-pod://, unix:// (or set DAGGER_ENGINE...)
ssh.note: The `ssh://` engine selector lets the CLI connect to a remote Dagger Engine over SSH; it is not an SSH login to an interactive sandbox machine. Debug access instead uses `dagger call -i`/`dagger terminal` (API-driven interactive terminal into a container), not SSH.

snapshot.quote: Package the container state as an OCI image, and publish it to a registry
snapshot.note: Container.publish/export capture filesystem state only as an OCI image; no memory/process-state snapshot exists.

snapshot_auto.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI.
snapshot_auto.note: Pipelines are ephemeral per-run; there is no automatic save/restore of a persistent machine's state on stop/sleep.

fork.quote: Container values are immutable, so any intermediate state can be reused to start new containers
fork.note: Dagger has no 'machine' to clone; its immutable, content-addressed container/build values let you reuse cached layers to start many new containers, which is caching/reuse, not a fork-a-running-machine feature.

fork_running.quote: The missing software stack for CI
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The missing software stack for CI
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

pause_resume.quote: Sending to a never-started agent starts it (signal-with-start).
pause_resume.note: The experimental Agent API can pause/resume Dagger's OWN LLM agent loop, not a customer 'machine'/engine instance for billing purposes. No machine-level pause/resume billing feature found.

wake_on_request.quote: The missing software stack for CI
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — engines run per pipeline invocation, not as an addressable always-present endpoint that wakes on request.

persistent_disk.quote: Constructs an engine-managed volume backed by operator-provided storage beneath the configured engine state root.
persistent_disk.note: CacheVolume/engineVolume persist data across pipeline runs on the engine host, so files can survive between runs, though there is no single persistent 'machine' disk in the VM sense.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — pipelines/containers are ephemeral per invocation rather than a persistent machine that idles and auto-stops.

live_resize.quote: The missing software stack for CI
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

agent_harnesses.quote: The missing software stack for CI
agent_harnesses.note: Dagger itself does not ship preinstalled coding-agent harness templates (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode). The related open-source tool container-use lets such harnesses use Dagger containers as sandboxes via MCP, but does not preinstall the harnesses themselves.

mcp_server.quote: It's an open-source MCP server that works as a CLI tool with Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible agents. Powered by Dagger.
mcp_server.note: container-use, built by the Dagger org and powered by the Dagger engine, is an MCP server that gives coding agents isolated container environments.

lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for writing/calling Dagger modules; any Python runtime is also available inside pipeline containers via images.

lang_node.quote: TypeScript and PHP still need an update to the new SDK interface.
lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/Node.js SDK exists for writing Dagger modules (sdk/typescript), alongside Node.js runtime availability inside pipeline containers via images.

public_ipv4.quote: Configures a hostname which can be used by clients within the session to reach this container.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: services are only reachable within the Dagger session by default; there is no per-machine public IPv4 assignment.

inbound_https.quote: Creates a tunnel that forwards traffic from the caller's network to this service.
inbound_https.note: Exposure requires an explicit local tunnel (Service.up/`dagger up`) mapping to the caller's own machine ports; there is no provider-hosted public HTTPS URL feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: The missing software stack for CI
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

guest_firewall.quote: containers, including nested engines, are in sibling `/buildkit` cgroups.
guest_firewall.note: Dagger's isolation is container-based (shared kernel), not a full VM/microVM with guest root network stack control, so the guest_firewall derivation used for full VMs does not apply.

static_egress_ip.quote: The missing software stack for CI
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed outbound IP feature documented; egress IP is whatever host runs the engine.

gpu.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no GPU machine offering found in docs/pricing.

windows.quote: containers, including nested engines, are in sibling `/buildkit` cgroups.
windows.note: The Dagger Engine executes containers on Linux (cgroups/buildkit); no Windows container/machine execution target is documented. The CLI is merely installable on Windows as a client.

macos.quote: containers, including nested engines, are in sibling `/buildkit` cgroups.
macos.note: not offered: engine executes Linux containers; the CLI is merely installable on macOS as a client, not a macOS machine execution target.

arm64.note: Dagger publishes multi-arch (amd64/arm64) engine and CLI images and runs on Apple Silicon/arm64 hosts; the engine and containers support the arm64 platform.

soc2.quote: We are excited to announce that Dagger has successfully received our SOC 2 Type II Report for the period of March 1 2024 - February 28 2025... clean audit opinion

hipaa.note: Trust Center lists only SOC 2 compliance; no HIPAA/BAA mention found on trust or pricing pages.

max_session_h.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI.
max_session_h.note: The self-hosted engine is a long-running daemon under the customer's control with no documented maximum session/runtime cap; individual pipeline runs are as long as the customer's own CI job allows.

egress_allowlist.quote: Dagger is the missing software stack for CI
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: Dagger is a CI orchestration/build engine (open-source, self-hosted, or early-access Cloud Engines for Cloud Checks); it has no product surface for provider-side outbound allow/deny lists or no-internet mode. Network egress from a Dagger container is whatever the host/network it runs on permits, not something Dagger's own docs, pricing, or compliance pages describe as a controllable platform feature.

byoc.note: The Enterprise plan offers a Dagger-managed single-tenant deployment (sales-only, no further detail published), not a documented option to deploy the managed service into the customer's own cloud account. The core engine is instead offered as self-hosted open source (self_host=true), which is a distinct model from BYOC.
